title: config-digger Agent definition
description: Where an Agent keeps its configuration, in which format, and with what precedence.

format_version.description: The version of this file format. Must be 1.

verified.description:
The lowest and highest versions of the Agent the real-Agent tests
passed on. Without it, the definition is untested, which every
Agent home of it notes.

installations.description: The launchable copies of the Agent, each with its own version.

last_ran.description:
Where the Agent records the version that last ran against an Agent
home, shown next to the Installations.

process.description:
How to tell that the Agent is running. Without it, config-digger
never finds it running.

homes.description: The Agent homes this Agent can have.

mirrored_homes.description:
Agent homes another tool copies from one of `homes`, such as the
Codex home Orca keeps in sync with `~\.codex`. config-digger reads
them and never writes to them.

lookup_orders.description:
The orders in which a launch of the Agent picks one of its homes,
each a list of home ids, such as the candidates for Claude Desktop's
data folder of each of its packages: it reads the first whose `when`
holds and whose folder exists, or that it uses before it exists. A
home some order holds and none picks is skipped, and shown as not
read. A home outside every order is read wherever it is found.

scopes.description:
The Scopes this Agent applies Entries at, in display order. A Scope is
only a label: precedence comes from the order of locations in `items`.

settings.description:
Sets of settings the Agent reads from the first of several sources
that holds any, such as managed settings.

projects.description: Where this Agent records the Projects it has been started on.

plugins.description:
The plugins this Agent installs, each in a folder of its own that
locations anchored in plugins are read in.

locations.description: The configuration locations this Agent reads.

feature_gates.description:
Switches on the Agent vendor's side that change how the Agent treats
its configuration, only those that change a State.

VerifiedRange.description:
A range of Agent versions, both ends included. Versions compare
numerically, component by component, padded with zeros; a pre-release
suffix counts as the numeric version it follows.

name.description: The display name, such as `Claude Code`.

notes.description:
What every Agent home of the Agent notes, such as configuration it
keeps only in the user's account.

DefinitionNote.description: Something every Agent home of an Agent notes, from a closed set.

oneOf.description:
The Agent's connectors live in the user's account, with no copy on
disk to list, such as Claude Desktop's.

The plugins the user installs for themself from the Agent's
marketplace live in the user's account, with no install record on
disk, such as Cursor's.

InstallationDefinition.description:
A launchable copy of the Agent, with its own version. It is found when
its executable exists, once per folder its `folder` glob matches.

id.description: A stable id, such as `native`, unique in the definition.

folder.description:
A glob of the folder it is in, starting with `~/`, `%NAME%` or a
drive; `*` and `?` stay within one folder name and `{a,b}` is
either, such as a version folder.

executable.description: The `/`-separated path of its executable, relative to its folder.

versions.description: Where its version is, tried in order: the first one read wins.

homes.description:
The ids of the Agent homes it reads. Omitted when it reads every
one. One that reads the first home also reads the homes the user
adds, which are laid out like it.

oneOf.description:
The product version in the version resource of an executable, such as
`claude.exe` or `Code.exe`. A fourth component of 0 is left out.

file.description:
A `/`-separated path relative to the Installation's folder, where
`*` and `?` stand for any name. Omitted for its executable.

oneOf.description: The `Version` of the `<Identity>` in an MSIX package's manifest.

file.description:
A `/`-separated path relative to the Installation's folder, where
`*` and `?` stand for any name. Omitted for `AppxManifest.xml`.

oneOf.description:
A string in a JSON file, such as `version` in a `package.json`, a
`product.json` or Codex's `codex-package.json`.

file.description:
A `/`-separated path relative to the Installation's folder, where
`*` and `?` stand for any name, such as a commit folder.

key_path.description: The key path of the string, one key per segment.

oneOf.description:
`DisplayVersion` in an uninstall key, such as an Inno Setup
`{<AppId>}_is1`: a fallback for an Installation whose files say nothing.

hive.description: The hive the key is in, for an install per user or per machine.

LastRan.description:
A string in a file of each Agent home: the version that last ran
against it, such as Claude Code's `lastReleaseNotesSeen`.

anchor.description: A JSON file of the Agent home.

key_path.description: The key path of the string, one key per segment.

Anchor.description: What a location's path is relative to.

oneOf.description: A root of the Agent home, or a path below it.

root.description: The name of a root declared by every home of the definition.

path.description:
A `/`-separated path relative to the root. Omitted when the root is
the location. In a Disable switch or a setting, `{plugin_id}` may
stand for the id of a plugin, such as Claude Desktop's
`Claude Extensions Settings/{plugin_id}.json`: there is then one file
per plugin, which applies to that plugin's Entries only.

oneOf.description: A path in the Project folder, and with `walk`, in its parents too.

path.description: A `/`-separated path relative to the Project folder.

walk.description:
Which folders the path is read in, from the Project folder up.
Only a location can walk.

oneOf.description:
A fixed path outside any Agent home or Project, read once for every
home of the Agent, such as a folder an organisation deploys to every
user of the machine, or one in the user's home folder that every home
of the Agent reads, such as VS Code's `~/.agents/skills`.

path.description:
Starts with `~/`, `%NAME%`, expanded from the environment, or a
drive; `/`-separated, without wildcards.

oneOf.description:
The settings a definition's `[[settings]]` names, in every file of each
of its sources. A location reads them all, and lists the Entries of the
sources the Agent skips as Unread; a rule or gate reads only the source
the Agent reads. Where one file is needed, it is refused.

A path in the folder of each plugin a definition's `[[plugins]]` lists,
read once per plugin.

plugins.description:
The id of a declared `[[plugins]]`, or several, such as Cursor's
plugins of a Project and its local ones, which it reads alike.

path.description:
A `/`-separated path relative to the plugin's folder, or several,
of which the first that exists is read, such as the first manifest
Cursor finds of `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` and
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.

oneOf.description:
A file in a folder above an Entry's own location, read once per Entry,
such as the `manifest.json` two folders above each skill Claude Desktop
mirrors from the account. Only a Disable switch is anchored here.

up.description:
How many folders up from the Entry's location, at least 1: 1 is the
folder holding it.

path.description: A `/`-separated path relative to that folder.

oneOf.description:
The workspace file a Project is, such as a `.code-workspace` file, read
once per such Project of an Agent that opens them.

A path in the folder the Agent home keeps for each Project, as the
definition's `json-folders` registry finds them, such as the
`state.vscdb` in each of VS Code's `workspaceStorage\<id>` folders. Its
Entries apply in that folder's Project only.

path.description: A `/`-separated path relative to the Project's folder of storage.

ProjectWalk.description: How far up from the Project folder a location in a Project is read.

oneOf.description: In the Project folder only.

In the Project folder and each parent up to the root of its git
repo, the folder holding `.git`. Outside a repo, in the Project
folder only.

PluginIds.description: The id of a declared `[[plugins]]`, or several.

ProcessDefinition.description:
How to tell that an Agent is running. It runs when a process matches
`images`, `paths` and `cmdline_contains`, or a session file names a PID
that is alive. Detection is best-effort: it warns or blocks a write, and
config-digger never closes an Agent.

images.description: Image names, such as `claude.exe`, compared case-insensitively.

paths.description:
Globs the executable's path must match one of, when set, such as
`~/.local/bin/claude.exe`: Claude Code and Claude Desktop are both
`claude.exe`. A glob starts with `~/`, `%NAME%` or a drive; `*` and
`?` stay within one folder name and `{a,b}` is either. Compared
case-insensitively. A process whose path the OS hides matches on its
image alone.

cmdline_contains.description:
Text the command line must contain, every one of them, compared
case-insensitively, such as Gemini CLI's script in `node.exe`. A
process whose command line the OS hides does not match: unlike a
path, it narrows down images such as `node.exe` that run much else.

session_files.description:
Files the Agent keeps per running session, each naming a PID that
counts only while it is alive.

SessionFiles.description: Files an Agent keeps for each running session, naming its PID.

oneOf.description:
One file per session directly in a folder, named `<pid>.<extension>`,
such as Claude Code's `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`. Only the names are
read, never the content, which can hold a Secret.

Locator.description: Where one root of an Agent home lives.

oneOf.description:
The user's home folder, written `~`, or a fixed path below it, written
`~/<relative path>`; or a path that starts with `%NAME%`, expanded from
the environment, or a drive, `/`-separated. Outside the user's home
folder, `*` and `?` stay within one folder name and `{a,b}` is either,
such as an MSIX package's folder: the path then names every existing
folder that matches.

The folder an environment variable holds, such as Claude Desktop's
`CLAUDE_USER_DATA_DIR`, while it is set to an absolute path. The Agent
uses it whenever it is set, creating it if needed.

The folders a list in a strict JSON file names, each relative to a base
folder, such as the VS Code profiles `userDataProfiles` in `storage.json`
lists below `User\profiles`. An item whose `unless` holds `true` names no
home of its own, such as a profile that shares its MCP servers with the
default profile, and nor does one whose folder is not a relative path.

file.description: The file. Starts with `%NAME%` or a drive; `/`-separated.

key_path.description: The key path of the list, one key per segment.

field.description: The field of an item that holds its folder, relative to `base`.

base.description: The folder the items' folders are in, written as `file` is.

unless.description: The key path in an item of a flag that, while `true`, leaves it out.

folder.description: The folder the home's roots are in.

roots.description:
Named roots of the home, each a `/`-separated path relative to its
folder. The home is found when any root exists. An Agent home the
user adds is laid out like the definition's first home.

process.description:
How to tell that the Agent of this home is running, in place of the
definition's `[process]`, such as for a home read by another
Installation of the Agent.

when.description:
Conditions under which the lookup order may pick the home, every one
of them, such as `%APPDATA%` being on a network share. Only a home
in the lookup order takes them.

default.description:
The home is the definition default, where the Agent keeps its
configuration unless told otherwise. At most one home is, and its
folder is one fixed path. Any other home found through a fixed path
or a search is found at a known location, and one an environment
variable names, through that variable.

HomeCondition.description: A condition under which an Agent reads a home of its lookup order.

oneOf.description:
Holds while an environment variable holds a path on a network share,
`\\server\share\…`, such as `%APPDATA%` in a redirected roaming profile.

MirroredHomeDefinition.description:
An Agent home whose content another tool copies from a source Agent
home, laid out like it. It is found, as a known location, when any of
its roots exists. A folder another home of the Agent finds too is this
home, whichever finds it.

owner.description: The tool that keeps the copy, as it names itself, such as `Orca`.

folder.description: The folder the home's roots are in.

source.description: The id of the home it copies, one of the definition's `homes`.

SettingsDefinition.description:
One set of settings, which the Agent reads from the first of its
sources that holds any setting, and from no other. Entries in the
others are Unread.

id.description: Unique in the definition, such as `managed`.

SettingsSource.description:
Where an Agent can read one set of its settings, such as the managed
settings an organisation deploys.

oneOf.description:
A string value in the Windows registry holding JSON, such as Claude
Code's `Settings` under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode`. It is shown
as `<HKLM|HKCU>\<key>\<value>`.

The values of a key in the Windows registry, each one setting, such as
Claude Desktop's policy under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude`. A string
value reads as a string, and a DWORD as `true` when it is 1 and `false`
when it is 0, as Windows policies store switches, and as its number
otherwise; a value of another type reads as `null`, holding a setting
config-digger does not read. It is shown as `<HKLM|HKCU>\<key>`.

A JSON file on the machine, and the `.json` files of a drop-in folder,
by name, read after it, such as Claude Code's `managed-settings.json`
and `managed-settings.d`. They are one source.

drop_ins.description: The drop-in folder, written as `path` is.

registries.description:
Each registry adds the Projects it records. Projects found by any Agent
are evaluated for every Agent.

workspace_files.description:
Whether the Agent opens `.code-workspace` files: such a Project
reads `project-file` locations in the file itself, and the other
locations in a Project in each of its member folders, the first
member ranking highest.

Registry.description: Where an Agent records the Projects it has been started on.

oneOf.description: The keys of an object in a strict JSON file, each one a Project.

anchor.description: Where the file is. It must not lie in a Project.

root.description: The key path of the object whose keys are Projects.

spelling.description: How the keys spell a Project. Omitted for paths.

oneOf.description:
A folder of the Agent home holding a folder per Project, each with a
strict JSON file naming its Project in the first of some fields, such as
VS Code's `workspaceStorage\<id>\workspace.json`, whose `folder` or
`workspace` is the Project. The Agent keeps what it stores for the
Project in that folder, which a `project-storage` anchor reads.

anchor.description: Where the folder of folders is. It must not lie in a Project.

file.description: The `/`-separated path of the file in each folder.

fields.description: The fields of the file that can name the Project, tried in turn.

spelling.description: How the fields spell a Project. Omitted for paths.

oneOf.description:
A list in the JSON text an Agent keeps under a key of the `ItemTable` of
a SQLite store, each item naming a Project in the first of some fields,
such as Cursor's `workspaceMetadata.entries`, whose `entries` each name
their folder in `folderUri`. The store is opened read-only and closed
straight after.

anchor.description: Where the store is. It must not lie in a Project.

key.description: The `ItemTable` key whose value is the JSON text.

list.description:
The key path of the list in the JSON, one key per segment. Omitted
when the JSON is the list.

fields.description:
The key paths in an item of the fields that can name its Project,
tried in turn.

spelling.description: How the fields spell a Project. Omitted for paths.

oneOf.description:
The keys of a table in a TOML file, each one a Project, such as the
folders Codex records a trust level for under `projects` in its
`config.toml`.

anchor.description: Where the file is. It must not lie in a Project.

root.description: The key path of the table whose keys are Projects.

oneOf.description:
Files of JSON lines below a folder, each naming the Project it was
written in on its first line, such as the `session_meta` line that opens
each Codex session's `rollout-*.jsonl`. A file whose first line is no
JSON object naming a folder records none.

anchor.description: Where the folder is. It must not lie in a Project.

files.description:
The `/`-separated path of the files below the folder, where `*` and
`?` stand for any name, such as `*/*/*/rollout-*.jsonl`.

fields.description:
The key paths in the first line of the fields that can name the
Project, tried in turn.

oneOf.description:
A column of a table of a SQLite store, each text value of it naming a
Project, such as the `cwd` of each thread Codex records in the `threads`
table of its `state_5.sqlite`. The store is opened read-only and closed
straight after. A store without the table records none.

anchor.description: Where the store is. It must not lie in a Project.

Spelling.description: How a registry spells a Project.

oneOf.description: A path, such as `E:\x` or `E:/x`.

A `file:` URI, such as `file:///e%3A/x`. A URI of any other scheme,
such as a remote folder's, names no Project on this machine.

PluginsDefinition.description:
Plugins an Agent installs, each in a folder of its own, such as Claude
Code's plugin cache. A plugin's Entries are Disabled with the whole
plugin through its own switch, and never Removed: the Agent uninstalls
it.

id.description: Unique in the definition, such as `installed`.

registry.description: Where the Agent records the plugins it installed.

superseded_marker.description:
A file whose presence in a plugin's folder means the Agent no longer
loads that folder, such as a version it superseded.

name.description:
Where a plugin's name is, or a list of places tried in turn, such as
an extension's `display_name`, then its `name`. When the plugin's
folder holds none, its name is its id up to `id_separator`.

id_separator.description:
The text that ends a plugin's name in its id, such as the `@` before
a marketplace. Without it, a plugin with no name is named by its id.

unique_names.description:
Whether the Agent names a plugin by its id when one before it, in
the registry's order, has its name, as Claude Desktop does with
extensions, so that their Entries never share a name.

uninstall.description:
The Agent's own command that uninstalls a plugin, shown in place of
Remove. `{id}` stands for the plugin's id, and `{scope}` for the
Scope it is installed at: when that is not recorded, the word
holding it and an option just before it are left out. Without it,
the Agent uninstalls a plugin only through its own interface.

PluginRegistry.description: Where an Agent records the plugins it installed.

oneOf.description:
An object in a strict JSON file whose keys are plugin ids, each holding
the plugin's records: an array of objects, one per Scope it is
installed at, or one object. A record without a folder is skipped.

anchor.description: Where the file is, in the Agent home.

root.description: The key path of the object whose keys are plugin ids.

folder.description: The field of a record that holds its folder.

scope.description: The field of a record that holds the Scope it is installed at.

project.description:
The field of a record that holds the path of the one Project it
applies in. Without it, a record applies in every Project.

version.description: The field of a record that holds its version.

oneOf.description:
The folders, in a folder of the Agent home or the machine, that hold a
marker file, each a plugin whose id is the folder's name, such as Claude
Desktop's extensions, each unpacked into `Claude Extensions\<id>` with
its `manifest.json`. A folder without a marker holds no plugin. Without
a marker, every folder whose name does not start with `.` is a plugin's,
such as Cursor's local plugins.

anchor.description: The folder the plugins' folders are in.

marker.description:
A `/`-separated path relative to a plugin's folder, or several, any
of which makes the folder a plugin's.

records.description: What the Agent records of each plugin it installed, when it does.

oneOf.description:
The keys of an object in a file of each Project folder, each a plugin
the Project installs from a marketplace, such as the `plugins` of
Cursor's `.cursor/settings.json`. A key is the plugin's name, or its
marketplace's and its name joined by `/`, and holds an object; the
plugin is named by the name. Its files are in a folder of a cache on
the machine, `<marketplace>/<name>/<version>`, the version being a
folder that holds the marker. The marketplace of a key that names none
is the first, by name, whose cache holds the plugin. A key whose plugin
is not in the cache installs nothing on disk yet, and is left out.

anchor.description: The file, in the Project folder.

dialect.description: The dialect the Agent reads the file in. Omitted for strict JSON.

root.description: The key path of the object whose keys are plugins.

scope.description: The Scope the plugins are recorded at, such as `project`.

cache.description: The folder of the cache, on the machine.

marker.description:
A `/`-separated path relative to a version folder whose presence
says the folder is complete, such as `.cache-complete`.

oneOf.description:
A cache of the Agent home holding each plugin it installed in
`<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>`, such as Codex's `plugins\cache`. A
plugin is named by its folder, its id is that name and its marketplace's
joined by `separator`, and its files are in its highest version, compared
number by number, or by text where either is no version. A folder whose
name starts with `.` is neither a marketplace, a plugin nor a version.

separator.description:
The text between a plugin's name and its marketplace's in its id,
such as `@`.

requires.description:
A `/`-separated path relative to a plugin's folder, above its
versions, that a plugin must hold to be listed here.

excludes.description:
A `/`-separated path relative to a plugin's folder, above its
versions, that a plugin must not hold to be listed here, such as the
file Codex writes beside a plugin the account installed.

InstallRecords.description:
An object in a strict JSON file of the Agent home whose keys are plugin
ids, each holding what the Agent recorded when it installed the plugin,
such as Claude Desktop's `extensions-installations.json`.

root.description: The key path of the object whose keys are plugin ids.

version.description: The field of a record that holds the version installed.

JsonDialect.description:
How much a reader accepts beyond strict JSON. A file one reader
rejects can still yield Entries for a reader with a looser dialect.

oneOf.description: No comments, no trailing commas.

`//` and `/* */` comments, and no trailing comma, such as Gemini
CLI's settings.
Comments and trailing commas, such as Cursor's and VS Code's files.

PluginNames.description: Where a plugin's name is: one place, or several tried in turn.

PluginName.description: A string in a JSON file of a plugin's folder that names the plugin.

file.description: A `/`-separated path relative to the plugin's folder.

key_path.description: The key path of the string, one key per segment.

root.description:
The key path of the object whose keys are Entries. One segment may be
`{project}`: each key there is a Project path, and the Entries below it
apply only in that Project. Any segment may be `*`, which stands for
every key there, such as each extension's servers in VS Code's cache.
Omitted for a folder of skill folders.

named_by.description:
When the value at `root` is a list of objects rather than an object
keyed by name, the field of each that holds its name, such as the
`label` of each server in VS Code's cache of extension servers. An
item without it is no Entry.

bare.description:
Whether a file without `root` holds its Entries at its top level
instead, as VS Code reads a `.mcp.json` that is a bare object of
servers.

one_entry.description:
Whether the value at `root` is one Entry rather than an object of
them, named by the plugin it is part of, such as the server a Claude
Desktop extension's manifest declares in `server.mcp_config`. Only a
location in plugins can hold one.

scope.description: The id of a declared Scope.

provenance.description: The base Provenance of the location's Entries.

store_class.description: How the location's file behaves while the Agent runs.

interpolation.description:
How the Agent writes references in this location's values. Without
it, every value is literal text.

secrets.description:
Fields of this location's Entries that hold Secrets, or that never
do, beyond what the core masks by default.

on_read_failure.description: What the Agent does when it cannot open, decode or parse the location.

risks.description:
How the Agent's own recovery from a Read failure here can lose
configuration, shown as warnings on the Read failure.

no_comments.description:
Whether config-digger keeps comments out of the location's file: it
writes none, not even those an Undo would put back above an Entry,
such as into Cursor's `mcp.json`, which a writer of Cursor's that
parses it as strict JSON empties when it holds one.

shape.description:
The minimal shape the Agent requires of the location's Entries:
one without it is Invalid. Without it, no Entry here is Invalid.

when.description:
Conditions under which the Agent reads the location, every one of
them. While one does not hold, its Entries are Unread.

name_template.description:
The name the Agent gives an Entry of the location, made of `{name}`,
the Entry's own name; in plugins, `{plugin}`, the plugin's name, such
as `{plugin}:{name}`; and in a Project, `{folder_index}`, the
position of the Entry's folder among those of the Project, 0 for a
folder Project, and `{folder}`, that folder's name, such as Cursor's
`project-{folder_index}-{folder}-{name}`. Without it, an Entry goes
by its own name.

switch_id.description:
What the Agent's Disable switches hold an Entry of this location by,
when not by its name, such as the server ids VS Code pairs with
`true` or `false` in `mcp.enablement`: a template of `{name}`, the
Entry's name; `{folder_index}`, the position of its folder among
those of the Project, 0 for a folder Project; `{uri_path}`, the path
of the `file:` URI of its file or skill folder, such as `/C:/x`;
`{skill_file}`, the absolute path of a skill's `SKILL.md`, the links
of its folder and of the folders above it resolved;
`{plugin_uri}`, the `file:` URI of its plugin's folder; and
`{extension}`, the key `*` stands for in its root up to a `/`, in
lower case.

references.description:
What the value at `root` of a location in plugins may hold besides
an object of Entries: a path, relative to the plugin's folder, of
another file in the location's format, or a list of such paths and
objects of Entries, such as a Claude Code plugin manifest's
`mcpServers`.

cached_at.description:
The key path, in the file as its format reads it, of when the Agent
cached the file's copy of configuration held elsewhere, such as the
bundle Codex caches from the account: milliseconds since 1970, or an
RFC 3339 time. Each Entry then carries a caveat that it is as of
then, or that the Agent does not record when, if the file does not
say. Omitted for a file the Agent reads as it is.

Format.description:
The format a location is read in: a file in a dialect, or a folder of
skill folders.

oneOf.description: JSON, in the dialect the Agent reads it in.
TOML.

A folder whose subfolders holding a `SKILL.md` are skills, each one an
Entry. A folder whose name starts with `.` is never read, and one
without `SKILL.md` is not an Entry.

recursive.description:
Whether a subfolder without `SKILL.md` is read in turn, at any depth.
A skill folder's own subfolders never are.

name_from.description: Where a skill's name comes from.

sanitize.description: How the Agent rewrites a name into the one it uses, if it does.

reserved.description:
Folder names the Agent never loads a skill from, compared
case-insensitively, such as a name it keeps for itself.

no_frontmatter.description:
What the Agent does with a `SKILL.md` that does not open with a
`---` frontmatter.

malformed_frontmatter.description: What the Agent does with a frontmatter that is not YAML it reads.

no_name.description:
What the Agent does with a frontmatter without a `name`, when
`name_from` is `frontmatter`.

oneOf.description:
The skill folders a list in a strict JSON file names, each by a path
relative to the file's folder to the skill folder or its `SKILL.md`, such
as the `contributes.chatSkills` of a VS Code extension's `package.json`.
Each is read as a folder of skill folders reads its skills.

list.description: The key path of the list.

field.description: The field of each item that holds the path.

skills.description: How each skill folder is read.

oneOf.description:
The skills a plugin's manifest declares in a field,
a path relative to the plugin's folder or a list of them, such as the
`skills` of a Cursor plugin's `plugin.json`. A path is a folder of skill
folders; an item of a list may instead name one skill folder or its
`SKILL.md`. A manifest that declares none, or a plugin with no
manifest, has its skills in the `default` folder instead. Only a
location in plugins, anchored at the manifest, reads them.

field.description: The key path of the field in the strict JSON manifest.

default.description: A `/`-separated path relative to the plugin's folder.

skills.description: How each folder of skill folders is read.

oneOf.description:
The JSON text an Agent keeps under a key of the `ItemTable` of a SQLite
store, such as VS Code's cache of extension servers under
`mcp.extCachedServers` in a workspace's `state.vscdb`. The store is
opened read-only, waiting briefly for an Agent that holds a write lock,
and closed straight after. The location's `root` starts with the key,
and config-digger never writes its Entries.

key.description: The `ItemTable` key whose value is the JSON text.

oneOf.description:
A strict JSON file holding lists of TOML texts, such as the bundle of
configuration Codex caches from the account in
`cloud-config-bundle-cache.json`. Each list is read as the one table its
texts fold into: tables merge key by key, and any other value of a
higher text replaces the lower one's whole. A text that is not TOML
makes the file fail to parse.

lists.description:
The key path of each list. An item is an object whose `contents`
holds its text.

contents.description: The field of an item that holds its text.

highest_first.description: Whether a list holds its highest text first, rather than last.

NameFrom.description: Where a skill's name comes from.

oneOf.description: The skill folder's name.
The `name` of the `SKILL.md` frontmatter.

Sanitize.description: How an Agent rewrites a skill's name.

oneOf.description:
Lower case, each run of characters other than `a`-`z` and `0`-`9`
replaced by one `-`, with no `-` at either end.

SkillFallback.description: What an Agent does with a skill whose `SKILL.md` it cannot fully read.

oneOf.description: It skips the skill, which is Invalid.

It loads the skill under its folder's name, with no other
frontmatter field: Effective, with a note.

SkillFolder.description:
A folder whose subfolders holding a `SKILL.md` are skills, each one an
Entry. A folder whose name starts with `.` is never read, and one
without `SKILL.md` is not an Entry.

recursive.description:
Whether a subfolder without `SKILL.md` is read in turn, at any depth.
A skill folder's own subfolders never are.

name_from.description: Where a skill's name comes from.

sanitize.description: How the Agent rewrites a name into the one it uses, if it does.

reserved.description:
Folder names the Agent never loads a skill from, compared
case-insensitively, such as a name it keeps for itself.

no_frontmatter.description:
What the Agent does with a `SKILL.md` that does not open with a
`---` frontmatter.

malformed_frontmatter.description: What the Agent does with a frontmatter that is not YAML it reads.

no_name.description:
What the Agent does with a frontmatter without a `name`, when
`name_from` is `frontmatter`.

Provenance.description: How the Entries of a location got there, which decides how they can be taken away.

oneOf.description:
A key someone wrote into a configuration file, or a skill folder
someone put there, by hand or through the Agent.

Configuration an organisation deploys to the machine, such as
enterprise skills. config-digger only reads it.

A copy the Agent keeps of configuration held in the user's account,
such as skills synced from claude.ai. config-digger only reads it.

Part of a plugin the Agent installed. config-digger Disables it only
through the plugin's own switch, with every Entry of the plugin, and
never Removes it: uninstalling is up to the Agent.

An extension the Agent installed, such as a Claude Desktop `.mcpb`,
read as a plugin is: config-digger Disables it only through its own
switch, and never Removes it.

Shipped with the Agent, which restores it as it ships it, such as
Cursor's built-in skills. config-digger only reads it.

Installed and switched on or off through the user's account, such
as the plugins Codex installs from the account's catalog: the Agent
takes their State from the account, not from a file. config-digger
only reads it.

StoreClass.description:
How a store config-digger writes behaves while its Agent runs, which
decides whether a write warns or is blocked then. Declared from the
weakest to the strongest: a file several locations read takes the
strongest of their classes.

oneOf.description:
A file the Agent reads and leaves alone: a write while it runs warns
that it may not see the change until it restarts.

A file the Agent rewrites from memory while it runs, such as
`~/.claude.json`: a write while it runs warns strongly that the Agent
may overwrite it.

A SQLite database the Agent holds open: a write while it runs is
blocked, whatever is acknowledged.

Interpolation.description:
How an Agent writes a reference to a value it reads elsewhere, such as an
environment variable. A value made only of references is not a Secret.

oneOf.description:
`${NAME}`, where `NAME` is a letter or `_` followed by letters, digits
and `_`, or one of `names` when they are set, plus
`${namespace:argument}` for each listed namespace, and
`${NAME<separator>default}` when a default separator is set, whose
default is literal text.

namespace_separator.description:
What comes between a namespace and its argument, such as the `.` of
a Claude Desktop extension's `${user_config.KEY}`. Omitted for `:`.

names.description:
The only names `${NAME}` stands for, such as VS Code's
`workspaceFolder` and `userHome`, or Cursor's `/`. Omitted for any
name.

SecretFields.description:
Key paths below an Entry, one key per segment, where `*` stands for any
key or array index.

fields.description:
Fields whose values are Secrets. Below an object or array, every
value is.

variable_names.description:
Fields that hold the name of a variable, such as Codex's
`bearer_token_env_var`: never a Secret, whatever else says so.

file_fields.description:
Key paths from the root of the file, outside any Entry, whose values
are Secrets, such as an API key stored next to the Entries. They are
masked wherever the file's text is shown, as in a diff's context lines.

encrypted_prefixes.description:
Prefixes the Agent writes before a value it encrypted, such as
Claude Desktop's `__encrypted__:`. Such a value is a Secret wherever
it is, in an Entry or anywhere in the file, and keeps its prefix.

ReadFailureReaction.description:
What an Agent does with a location it cannot read. Declared from the
mildest to the strongest: a file several locations of one Agent read
takes the strongest of their reactions.

oneOf.description: It starts without the location's Entries.

It asks the user at startup what to do with the file, and otherwise
starts without its Entries.

What it does is not known: every Item in the contexts the location
reaches gets a caveat.
It refuses to start in the contexts the location reaches.

RiskCode.description: How an Agent's own recovery from a Read failure can lose configuration.

oneOf.description: It may offer to reset the file, losing what it holds.
It may write the file again from empty, dropping its Entries.
It may clear the sign-in state of servers that vanish.

Shape.description: The minimal shape of the Entries of a location.

oneOf.description:
An object that holds at least one of some fields, each field it holds
being of the type the Agent reads.

one_of.description: The Entry must hold at least one of these, such as `command` or `url`.

types.description: The type of each field, when the Entry holds it.

still_competes.description: Whether an Entry without this shape still competes by name.

FieldType.description: The type of a field's value.

oneOf.description: A list of strings.
An object whose values are strings.

Condition.description: A condition under which an Agent reads a location.

oneOf.description:
Holds while a Feature gate of the same definition is on, or with
`is = false`, while it is off.

gate.description: The name of a declared Feature gate.

is.description: The value the gate must have. Omitted for on.

oneOf.description:
Whether a setting the Agent reads in layers has a value: the first of
its sources that holds it decides, and the Agent's default stands when
none does.

sources.description:
Where the setting is, highest first, such as a folder's settings
before the user's.

default.description: The value the Agent takes when no source holds the setting.

SettingPlace.description:
A value an Agent reads from one of its settings files, such as the list
a rule holds. config-digger only reads it.

key_path.description:
The key path of the value. One segment may be `{project}`: the
context's Project key, in the Agent's own spelling, so that the
value applies only there.

policy.description:
The value is managed policy: what it keeps out is Blocked, by
`policy`, rather than Disabled.

dialect.description: The dialect the Agent reads the file in. Omitted for strict JSON.

sqlite.description:
Whether the file is a SQLite store, such as VS Code's `state.vscdb`,
whose `ItemTable` holds JSON text under the key path's first key.

toml.description: Whether the file is TOML, such as Codex's `config.toml`, rather than JSON.

fragments.description:
How a strict JSON file holding lists of TOML texts is read, such as
the bundle Codex caches from the account, rather than as JSON.

cached_at.description:
The key path, in the same file, of when the Agent cached the value:
milliseconds since 1970, or an RFC 3339 time, such as when VS Code
fetched the account's policy. Omitted for a value the user writes.

map.description:
How the Agent reads the value as the setting's, as `[held, read]`
pairs, such as VS Code reading a policy's `mcp: false` as
`chat.mcp.access: "none"`. A value no pair holds then sets nothing.
Omitted, the value is read as it is.

TomlFragments.description:
A strict JSON file holding lists of TOML texts, such as the bundle of
configuration Codex caches from the account in
`cloud-config-bundle-cache.json`. Each list is read as the one table its
texts fold into: tables merge key by key, and any other value of a
higher text replaces the lower one's whole. A text that is not TOML
makes the file fail to parse.

lists.description:
The key path of each list. An item is an object whose `contents`
holds its text.

contents.description: The field of an item that holds its text.

highest_first.description: Whether a list holds its highest text first, rather than last.

References.description:
Files a value can point to, each holding Entries in the format of the
location that holds the value.

root.description: The key path of the object whose keys are Entries in a file pointed to.

precedence.description: Location ids of this kind, highest precedence first.

merge.description:
How the Agent combines same-named Entries into the one it uses, field
by field. Omitted, the highest wins whole and Shadows the others.

checks.description:
The Agent's checks, in the order it applies them: an Entry's State
comes from the first it fails, and the others it fails are listed as
secondary reasons. Each check appears once.

disable.description:
How the Agent Disables an Entry, in its order of preference. Disable
uses the most specific one (target, then context) that covers the
Entry and applies in the context, taking the first in this order
among equally specific ones, and skipping any whose switch is
git-versioned.

gates.description:
What keeps the Agent from using an Entry whatever it declares, such
as managed policy: config-digger never lifts these.

rules.description:
Settings that keep Entries out by a rule rather than one by one,
such as deny lists: config-digger never writes them.

Competition.description: How same-kind Entries of one Agent home compete.

oneOf.description:
Entries compete when their names are exactly equal. An Entry of a
`by_endpoint` location competes instead with the Entries of other
locations that have its endpoint, joining the Item of the one the Agent
ranks highest, and otherwise with those of `by_endpoint` locations that
have it.

by_endpoint.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries compete by endpoint, such as
Claude Code's plugin servers.

oneOf.description:
Entries compete when their names are equal without regard to case, as
VS Code compares server labels, and with `only_while`, only while a
setting has a value, such as VS Code's `chat.mcp.collisionBehavior`.

only_while.description:
The setting Entries compete only while it holds. Omitted, they
always do.

oneOf.description:
Entries compete when they lie at the same path below the same folder,
whatever their names, once each path is cut at the first of `markers` it
passes through, as Cursor compares skills: `~\.claude\skills\review` and
`~\.agents\skills\review` both lie at `skills\review` below `~`, while
`~\.claude\skills\x\review` does not. Paths compare without regard to
case. An Entry whose path passes through no marker competes with none.

Entries compete when their names are exactly equal, except that, while
the Feature gate `gate` is on, the remote Entries of `locations` compete
by URL instead, as Cursor runs one server per URL: the one the Agent ranks
highest wins. A remote Entry has a `url` and no `command`.
URLs compare as WHATWG URLs, by scheme, host and port, path without a
trailing `/`, and query, a URL without a scheme taking `http://`.

locations.description: The ids of the locations whose remote Entries compete by URL.

gate.description:
The name of a declared Feature gate, which must list `locations` in
its `affects`.

unseen.description:
What else takes part that config-digger cannot see, which every
Entry that competes by URL notes.

oneOf.description:
Entries never compete: each is an Item of its own, whatever its name, as
Codex lists every skill it finds, same-named ones included.

SettingIs.description:
Whether a setting the Agent reads in layers has a value: the first of
its sources that holds it decides, and the Agent's default stands when
none does.

sources.description:
Where the setting is, highest first, such as a folder's settings
before the user's.

default.description: The value the Agent takes when no source holds the setting.

UnseenServers.description: Servers an Agent counts that config-digger cannot see.

oneOf.description: Those extensions give the Agent while it runs.
Those the user's team configures for them.

Those of the plugins the user installs from a marketplace, which
the Agent keeps in the user's account.
The one the user picked among those with the same URL.

Merge.description:
How an Agent combines same-named Entries into the one server it uses,
rather than letting the highest win whole. Each Entry that takes part is
Merged, and the Item shows the server built, with the Entry each field
comes from.

oneOf.description:
Tables merge key by key at any depth, from the lowest Entry up, and any
other value of a higher Entry replaces the lower one's whole, arrays
included, as Codex folds `[mcp_servers.<name>]` across its layers. An
Entry may hold only some fields, such as only `enabled = false`.

exclusive.description:
Fields of which the built server may hold one at most, such as
Codex's `command` and `url`: holding more, it is rejected, every
Entry that takes part is Invalid, and the Agent is flagged as unable
to start in the context.

enabled.description:
The field whose `false` in the built server turns it off, such as
Codex's `enabled`: every Entry of the Item is then Disabled, by the
Entry the field comes from.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries merge, such as Codex's
`config.toml` layers. Omitted, every location of the Item kind
merges. The server built from them competes whole with the Entries
of the others, which rank below them, such as a plugin's server of
the same name.

Check.description: One of an Agent's checks that decides an Entry's State.

oneOf.description:
A managed file takes exclusive control and leaves the Entry out, or
a field the organisation sets keeps it out: Blocked, with `policy`.
A Blocked Entry does not compete. Required when a gate of the kind
is managed-exclusive or a policy field, and refused otherwise.
A Disable mechanism's switch is set for the Entry: Disabled.

The Agent has not approved the Entry: Blocked, with `not_approved`.
Required when a gate of the kind is an approval list, an approval
hash or a nonce trust, and refused otherwise.

The user has not trusted the Entry's Project: Blocked, with
`untrusted_folder`. Required when a gate of the kind is trusted
folders, and refused otherwise.

A rule keeps the Entry out: Blocked, with `policy`, when the rule is
managed policy, and Disabled, with `disabled_by_rule` or
`disabled_globally`, otherwise. Before `precedence`, an Entry a rule
keeps out does not compete; after it, a rule applies to the Entry
that wins, which still beats the others. Required when the kind has
rules, and refused otherwise.

A same-named Entry the Agent ranks higher is not Disabled: Shadowed.
Where the kind merges, each Entry that takes part, with another, in
the server the Agent builds is Merged instead.

The server the Agent builds from the Item's Entries holds fields that
exclude each other: every Entry that takes part is Invalid, with
`transport_conflict`. Required when the kind merges, and refused
otherwise.

The Entry lacks the minimal shape its location declares: Invalid.
Required when a location of the kind declares a shape, and refused
otherwise.

The Agent skips the skill because of its `SKILL.md` or its folder's
name: Invalid. Required when a location of the kind is a folder of
skill folders, and refused otherwise.

DisableMechanism.description:
How an Agent Disables an Entry. An Item kind lists its mechanisms in
the Agent's order of preference.

oneOf.description:
A list of names in a JSON file: the Agent skips every Entry of an Item
whose name is in it. Disable appends the name, creating the list and
any missing parent; Enable removes it.

enable_offered.description:
Whether config-digger writes the switch: Disable through it, and
Enable lifting it. Off for a switch it only reads, such as one in a
file shared with a team or applying to every Project.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries it Disables. Omitted, it
Disables Entries of every location of the Item kind.

when.description:
Feature gates under which the Agent reads the switch, every one of
them, such as one that moves it to another store. While one does not
hold, the switch Disables nothing and Disable skips it.

oneOf.description:
A field in a JSON file whose value says whether the Agent skips an
Entry, such as `enabled: false`. Disable sets it to `disabled_value`,
adding it and any missing parent; Enable deletes it or sets it to
`enabled_value`, as `enable_action` says.

switch.description: The field. Its key path may hold `{name}`, the Entry's name.

disabled_value.description: The value that Disables the Entry.

default_value.description:
The value the Agent takes while the field, or its file, is missing,
such as `false` for Claude Desktop's `isEnabled`, which an extension
without a settings file has. Of layered fields, the Agent takes the
last one's while no layer holds a value. Omitted, a missing field
Disables nothing.

partial_values.description:
Values that are partial switches, limiting part of the Entry, such
as a skill listed by name only: the Entry stays Effective, with a note.

enable_offered.description:
Whether config-digger writes the switch: Disable through it, and
Enable lifting it. Off for a switch it only reads, such as one in a
file shared with a team or applying to every Project.

layered.description:
Whether the field is one layer of a setting the Agent merges across
files, such as Claude Code's `enabledPlugins`: among the layered
mechanisms of the Item kind, in the definition's order, the first
whose field holds a value for the Entry decides.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries it Disables. Omitted, it
Disables Entries of every location of the Item kind.

when.description:
Feature gates under which the Agent reads the switch, every one of
them, such as one that moves it to another store. While one does not
hold, the switch Disables nothing and Disable skips it.

plugin_scopes.description:
With target `plugin`, the Scopes a plugin must be installed at for
the field to apply to it, as the Agent records them, such as Cursor
reading a user install's `enabledPlugins` in the user settings alone.
Omitted, it applies to every plugin.

oneOf.description:
A list in a JSON value holding an item per Entry it switches, each named
by its `named_by` field or index, such as the `[id, enabled]` pairs of
VS Code's `mcp.enablement` or the skill files of its
`chat.disabledPromptFiles.skill`. An Entry is held by the id its
location's `switch_id` makes, and the switch's key path ends in
`{name}`, standing for its item. The Agent skips an Entry whose item is
there and is not `enabled_item`. Disable replaces the item with
`disabled_item`, creating the list and any missing parent; Enable takes
it away, or with `set`, replaces it with `enabled_item`.

switch.description: The list, `{name}` standing for the Entry's item in it.

disabled_item.description:
The item Disable writes, each string `{name}` in it standing for the
Entry's id, such as `["{name}", false]`.

enabled_item.description:
The item that Enables the Entry, likewise, such as `["{name}", true]`,
which beats an item of a later layer. Enable writes it with
`enable_action = "set"`.

ignore_case.description:
Whether the Agent compares ids without regard to case, as it
compares Windows paths.

enable_offered.description:
Whether config-digger writes the switch: Disable through it, and
Enable lifting it.

layered.description:
Whether the list is one layer of a setting the Agent merges across
stores, such as VS Code's `mcp.enablement` in a workspace's store over
the profile's: among the layered mechanisms of the Item kind, in the
definition's order, the first whose list holds the Entry decides.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries it Disables. Omitted, it
Disables Entries of every location of the Item kind.

when.description:
Feature gates under which the Agent reads the switch, every one of
them, such as one that moves it to another store. While one does not
hold, the switch Disables nothing and Disable skips it.

oneOf.description:
Disables a server the Agent builds from same-named Entries by writing
`false` to the field its merge turns servers off by, such as Codex's
`enabled`, in the Entry's own table. The field merges like any other, so
what it Disables is every Entry of the Item, and a higher layer that sets
the field decides over a lower one. Enable is left to the merge's own
rules.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries it Disables, each one that
merges.

requires_unset_above.description:
Whether a write counts only while no higher layer sets the field,
such as Codex's: Disable skips a layer below one that sets it.

fallback.description:
The id of the location that takes a table holding the field alone,
named as the Entry is, when the Entry's own file is git-versioned or
read only, such as Codex's user `config.toml`. Omitted, such an Entry
has no Disable.

oneOf.description:
Disables an Entry that has no switch of its own, such as a server in
Claude Desktop's user file or a skill in Cursor, by moving it out of the
Agent's reach into config-digger's parked-Entry store, where it stays
listed as Disabled; Enable puts it back (ADR 0002). Disable prefers any
switch to it, and never parks an Entry in a git-versioned file or folder.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries it parks: each a file outside
any plugin, holding Entries under keys, or a folder of skill folders
outside any plugin.

Switch.description: The key a mechanism writes, in a JSON file outside or inside a Project.

anchor.description:
The file. Its path may name `{plugin_id}` instead of the key path,
for a file per plugin.

key_path.description:
The key path of the value written. One segment may be `{project}`:
the context's Project key, in the Agent's own spelling, so that the
switch applies only there. One segment after it may be `{name}`,
the Entry's name, or `{plugin_id}`, the id of the plugin it is part
of, or both, `{plugin_id}` first, for a switch of each Entry of a
plugin, such as Codex's `plugins.<id>.mcp_servers.<name>.enabled`.

named_by.description:
When the value where `{name}` stands is a list of objects rather
than an object keyed by name, the field of each that holds its name,
such as `name` in the `skills` of the manifest of Claude Desktop's
skill mirror. config-digger only reads such a switch.

later_wins.description:
With `named_by`, whether of several items naming an Entry the
Agent takes the last, such as the rules of Codex's
`[[skills.config]]`, rather than the first.

store_class.description:
How the switch's file behaves while the Agent runs. A `sqlite` file
is a SQLite store, such as VS Code's `state.vscdb`, whose `ItemTable`
holds JSON text under the key path's first key.

dialect.description:
The dialect the Agent reads the file in, such as Cursor's JSONC
`.cursor/settings.json`. Omitted for strict JSON.

toml.description: Whether the file is TOML, such as Codex's `config.toml`, rather than JSON.

MechanismTarget.description:
What one write of a mechanism's switch Disables. Declared from the most
specific to the widest: Disable prefers the most specific mechanism.

oneOf.description: The one Entry.
Every Entry of the Item it covers, since they share the name.

Every Entry of the plugin the Entry is part of, of every Item kind.
The switch's key path names the plugin with `{plugin_id}`, and it
covers locations in plugins only.

MechanismContext.description:
Where a mechanism's switch applies. Declared from the most specific to
the widest: Disable prefers the most specific mechanism.

oneOf.description: In one Project: the switch is in a Project folder, or keyed by `{project}`.
In every context.

EnableAction.description: What Enable writes to lift a mechanism's switch.

oneOf.description: Removes the name from the list.
Deletes the key.
Sets the key to the mechanism's `enabled_value`.

DisableReason.description: The reason code an Entry Disabled through a mechanism gets.

oneOf.description:
The switch names the Item, so every Entry of it that the mechanism
covers is Disabled.
The switch is the Entry's own.

The switch is that of the plugin the Entry is part of, so every
Entry of the plugin is Disabled.

Gate.description:
Something outside an Entry that keeps the Agent from using it, which
Enable cannot lift and config-digger never lifts: the Entry is Blocked.

oneOf.description:
A managed file that takes exclusive control while it exists, even
empty: the Agent then loads no Entry of the kind from any other
location but those it exempts, which are Blocked by `policy`. Such as
Claude Code's `managed-mcp.json`.

location.description: The id of the location whose file takes control, outside any Project.

except.description:
The ids of the other locations it leaves alone, such as servers the
managed settings declare.

oneOf.description:
Entries the Agent uses only once the user approves them, such as Claude
Code's `.mcp.json` servers: one no source approves is Blocked, with
`not_approved`. config-digger never approves an Entry.

locations.description: The ids of the locations whose Entries need approval.

sources.description:
Where approvals are: a list of the names approved, or `true`,
which approves every Entry.

prompt.description: Where the Agent asks the user to approve an Entry.

oneOf.description:
A field an organisation sets to keep an Entry out, such as the
`orgBlockedReason` Claude Desktop writes into the settings of an
extension on its organisation's blocklist: while a source holds anything
but `null`, `false` or `""` there, the Entry is Blocked by `policy`.

locations.description: The ids of the locations whose Entries it can Block.

oneOf.description:
Locations whose Entries the Agent uses only in a Project the user trusts,
such as the servers of a workspace VS Code reads only once its Workspace
Trust is given: an Entry of one in a Project the user has not trusted is
Blocked, with `untrusted_folder`. A folder is trusted when an item of a
source trusts it or a folder above it, and a workspace file when it and
each of its folders are. config-digger never trusts a folder.

locations.description: The ids of the locations whose Entries need trust, each in a Project.

sources.description: Where the lists of trusted folders are, every one of them read.

uri.description:
The field of an item that holds the folder's `file:` URI, as text
or as VS Code's URI object.

trusted.description:
The field of an item that must hold `true` for it to trust the
folder. Omitted, every item trusts its folder.

trust_all.description:
A setting that, while it is met, trusts every folder, such as VS
Code's `security.workspace.trust.enabled: false`.

oneOf.description:
Entries the Agent uses only once the user trusts them, and asks about
again whenever their configuration changes, such as the servers VS Code
discovers in other apps' files: one no source trusts is Blocked, with
`not_approved`. A source holds a list of `[id, record]` pairs, each id
as the location's `switch_id` makes it, and the Entry is trusted while
its record's `trusted_at` field equals its `nonce` field. config-digger
cannot tell whether the configuration changed since the Agent recorded
the nonce, and never trusts an Entry.

locations.description: The ids of the locations whose Entries need trust.

sources.description: Where the lists of records are, every one of them read.

trusted_at.description: The field of a record holding the nonce the user trusted.

nonce.description:
The field of a record holding the nonce of the configuration the
Agent last saw.

oneOf.description:
Entries the Agent uses only once the user approves them as they are
configured, such as Cursor's Project servers: a source holds a list of
`<id>:<hash>` texts, each id as the location's `switch_id` makes it, or
else the Entry's name, and each hash that of the configuration approved;
a bare `<id>` approves the Entry however it is configured. One no source
approves is Blocked, with `not_approved`, so that changing an approved
Entry Blocks it again. config-digger never approves an Entry.

locations.description: The ids of the locations whose Entries need approval.

sources.description: Where the lists of approvals are, every one of them read.

hash.description: How the Agent hashes an Entry's configuration.

prompt.description: Where the Agent asks the user to approve an Entry.

oneOf.description:
Locations in each folder from a Project's root down to its own folder
that the Agent reads only once the user trusts a folder, as Codex reads a
`<folder>\.codex\config.toml`: it looks up the folder itself, then the
Project's root, the folder holding `.git`, then the main checkout of its
git repository, among the keys of a table of folders, and the first it
finds with a trust level decides. An Entry of a folder whose level is not
`trusted`, or that none of them has, is Blocked, with `untrusted_folder`.
Keys compare as paths, without regard to case. config-digger never
trusts a folder.

locations.description: The ids of the locations whose Entries need trust, each in a Project.

sources.description:
Where the tables of folders are, each keyed by a folder's path,
highest first: the first that gives a folder a trust level decides.

field.description: The field of a folder's record that holds its trust level.

trusted.description: The trust level that trusts the folder.

ApprovalPrompt.description: Where an Agent asks the user to approve an Entry.

oneOf.description: When it starts in the Project.
In its settings of MCP servers.

ConfigHash.description:
How an Agent hashes an Entry's configuration to tell whether it changed
since the user approved it. config-digger computes it from the Entry as
written, Secrets included, and never shows it.

oneOf.description:
Cursor's: VS Code's 32-bit string hash, written in hexadecimal with
a `-` when negative, of the JSON text of the fields of the server's
transport, in this order: its `command`, `args`, `env` and `envFile`
when it has a `command`, and otherwise its `url`, given `http://`
when it names no scheme, `headers` and `auth`.

Rule.description:
A setting that keeps Entries out by a rule rather than one by one, such
as a deny list: the Entries it keeps out are Disabled, or Blocked when
the setting is policy. config-digger never writes it, so Enable is not
offered.

oneOf.description:
Lists of servers, each item naming servers by name, command or URL,
merged from every source that holds one. A deny list keeps out every
server an item matches. An allow list, once any source holds one, keeps
out every server no item matches: an empty one keeps out all of them.

sources.description:
Where the lists are. A server an allow list keeps out is Blocked
when any allow list is policy.

match.description: The field of an item that matches each part of a server.

policy_only.description:
A setting that, while it holds `true`, leaves only the allow lists
of policy sources, such as Claude Code's `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`.

strict.description:
When the allow list holds an item matching by command, a server
with a command is allowed only by such an item, and when it holds
one matching by URL, a remote server only by such an item.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries it covers. Omitted, it covers
every location of the Item kind.

oneOf.description:
A setting that turns off every Entry it covers while it holds `off`,
such as Claude Code's `syncClaudeAiSkills: false`. The first source
that holds it decides, or with `every_source`, the first that holds
`off`; the Entries are Disabled globally, or Blocked when that source is
policy.

off.description: The value that turns the Entries off.

every_source.description:
Whether every source must leave the Entries on, as when the Agent
loads them only while neither its policy nor its own file holds
`off`, such as Claude Desktop's `isLocalDevMcpEnabled`.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries it covers. Omitted, it covers
every location of the Item kind.

oneOf.description:
Tables of the servers an organisation allows, each keyed by a server's
name and holding what that server must be, such as the `mcp_servers` of
Codex's `requirements.toml`: `identity = { command = "…" }` or
`identity = { url = "…" }`. The tables of every source merge name by
name, a higher source's winning. Once any source holds a table, a server
whose name it lacks, or whose command or URL is not the one its name
requires, is kept out. A requirement held some other way, such as a
table matching a command's args, is not read: its server is taken to
meet it.

sources.description:
Highest first. A server they keep out is Blocked when any source
holding a table is policy.

identity.description: The field of a server's requirement holding what it must be.

per_plugin.description:
For sources whose value is keyed by plugin id, the key path in each
plugin's value of its table, such as the `mcp_servers` of Codex's
`[plugins."<id>"]`: a plugin's server meets only its own plugin's
table, and once any plugin has one, the servers of a plugin with
none are kept out. Omitted, a source's value is the table.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries it covers. Omitted, it covers
every location of the Item kind.

ListKind.description: Whether a list keeps out what it matches or what it does not.

ItemFields.description:
The fields of a list item, each matching one part of a server on the
common server model.

name.description: Holds a server name, matched exactly.

command.description: Holds the command and its args as one list, matched exactly.

url.description: Holds a URL, where `*` stands for any text.

FeatureGateDefinition.description:
A switch on the Agent vendor's side, such as whether Claude Code syncs
skills from claude.ai. config-digger sees at most the value the Agent
last cached, shown as of when it cached it; otherwise it assumes the
Agent's default. Every Entry it affects gets a caveat saying which.

name.description: The gate's name as the vendor knows it, unique in the definition.

assumed.description: The value the Agent uses when it has none cached.

affects.description: The ids of the locations whose Entries depend on it.

lookup.description: Where the Agent caches the gate's value.

bypass.description: When the Agent ignores its cache and uses its own default.

GateLookup.description: Where an Agent caches a Feature gate's value.

oneOf.description:
A gate's value in a JSON file of the Agent home, such as Claude Code's
`cachedGrowthBookFeatures` in `~/.claude.json`.

anchor.description: The file, in the Agent home.

key_path.description:
The key path of the gate's `true` or `false`, one key per segment.
One segment is `{gate}`: the gate's name, or its hash with `hash`.

hash.description:
How the Agent hashes gate names in its cache. Omitted when it keys
them by name.

cached_at.description:
The key path of when the Agent cached its values: milliseconds
since 1970, or an RFC 3339 time. Omitted when it records none.

oneOf.description:
A gate's value in the JSON text an Agent keeps under a key of the
`ItemTable` of a SQLite store, as VS Code and Cursor keep their state in
`state.vscdb`, such as Cursor's Statsig bootstrap.

anchor.description: The SQLite file, in the Agent home.

key.description: The `ItemTable` key whose value is the JSON text.

key_path.description:
The key path of the gate's `true` or `false` in the JSON, one key
per segment. One segment is `{gate}`: the gate's name, or its hash
with `hash`.

hash.description:
How the Agent hashes gate names in its cache. Omitted when it keys
them by name.

cached_at.description:
The key path in the JSON of when the Agent cached its values:
milliseconds since 1970, or an RFC 3339 time. Omitted when it
records none.

GateHash.description: How an Agent hashes gate names in its cache.

oneOf.description:
Statsig's djb2: a 32-bit hash of the name's UTF-16 code units,
written as an unsigned decimal number.

Bypass.description: When an Agent ignores its cached Feature gate values.

oneOf.description:
Environment variables that make the Agent ignore its cache, such as
Claude Code's `DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK`.

variables.description: The cache is ignored when any of them is set.

env_maps.description:
Maps of variables the Agent applies over the environment it starts
in, such as the `env` of Claude Code's user settings, highest
first. A variable there replaces the one in the environment.

BypassVariable.description: One variable that makes the Agent ignore its cache.

unless.description:
Variables that, when any is set to a non-empty value, keep this one
from counting.

VariableValues.description: Which values of a variable count as setting it.

oneOf.description: Any non-empty value, `0` and `false` included.
`1`, `true`, `yes` or `on`, in any case.

EnvMap.description:
A JSON object of variable names and string values in a file of the
Agent home or the machine, such as the `env` of a settings file.

key_path.description: The key path of the object, one key per segment.
